headline: GitLab’s 10.0 RCE leads active-exploitation day
standfirst: A maximum-severity GitLab flaw already exploited against Alpine Linux, active Drupal Commerce Core exploitation and mass WordPress scanning dominate the vulnerability agenda, while Binance discloses a multi-billion-dollar security incident and a trojanized AI coding extension exposes developer supply-chain risk. Cisco SD-WAN and TeamViewer flaws and an FBI seizure round out the picture.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

GitLab CE/EE contains a CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-97229, fixed in 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2; the supplied NVD entry ties it to insufficient validation of a specially crafted regular expression in CI/CD configuration. It is confirmed in CISA KEV and the source reports exploitation against Alpine Linux; the supplied CVSS vector indicates no privileges or user interaction are required [[s28]].

Drupal Commerce Core’s missing-authorization flaw, CVE-2026-118539, affects versions 0.0.0 through 2.41 and 3.0.0 through 3.3.13; Drupal warns it is being actively exploited, though no CVSS value is supplied and CISA KEV enrichment shows no catalog match [[s34]].

WordPress Core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 face a high-severity RCE, CVSS 8.1 and no CVE identifier, with nearly 63,000 attack attempts in 24 hours shortly after patches appeared [[s11]]. Analysis: the attempt count indicates mass scanning, not necessarily successful compromise; the source does not supply exploit prerequisites.

## Breaches

Binance says a security incident affected about $6.3 billion in assets, with nearly $3 billion frozen on-chain; Tether and Circle froze more than 1.567 billion USDT and 800 million USDC respectively [[s36]]. The supplied account gives no cause, attribution or customer-loss confirmation; the operational question is how much remains exposed. Analysis: the stablecoin freezes are the clearest containment lever described, but they do not establish a root cause.

Separately, a malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor’s marketplace for about 11 hours, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware that installed persistent SSH backdoors [[s8]]. No CVE or technical root cause is supplied. Analysis: the incident makes AI-assisted development tooling a supply-chain target; the source does not say whether the backdoors were used.

## Research

UAT-11473, described as a newly identified APT group, exploited CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator to deploy a custom KeyDrift framework [[s47]]. The authentication bypass is CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated and remote, and can yield internal high-privileged access and NETCONF configuration control; CISA lists it in KEV, and the supplied NVD ranges cover multiple releases, including branches before 20.9.8.2 and 20.16 before 20.18.2.1. Analysis: pairing a control-plane bypass with bespoke malware suggests the access is being used for persistence, not just initial entry; the source does not describe KeyDrift’s capabilities beyond the framework label.

## Vulnerabilities

TeamViewer Full Client, Portable and Remote Control App before 15.83 contain CVE-2026-111585, an integer overflow in remote-control screen processing rated CVSS 8.8 High [[s31]]. Exploitation requires the user to establish a remote-control session to an attacker-controlled or compromised host and can cause denial of service or, depending on platform, code execution with viewer privileges. The flaw is not listed in KEV. Analysis: the direction of attack turns a support session against the technician’s machine, but the user-initiated session requirement limits mass exploitation.

## Industry

The FBI seized the domain of Virtualine, a bulletproof host that the source says catered to hack-for-hire services, supported ransomware and infostealer operators, and accepted crypto payments [[s14]]. No arrest, charge or customer count is supplied. Analysis: domain seizure disrupts a named service but does not by itself show the underlying criminal operations have been dismantled.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, contain an authentication bypass vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system. This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.
kev.requiredAction: Please adhere to CISA’s guidelines to assess exposure and mitigate risks associated with Cisco SD-WAN devices as outlines in CISA’s Emergency Directive 26-03 (URL listed below in Notes) and CISA’s “Hunt & Hardening Guidance for Cisco SD-WAN Devices (URL listed below in Notes). Adhere to the applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are not available.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the peering authentication in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Validator, formerly SD-WAN vBond, could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system.

This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.

selected.angle: UAT-11473 pairing the long-known CVE-2026-20127 SD-WAN authentication bypass with a custom KeyDrift framework shows controllers remain a durable APT foothold.

nvd.description: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.
